newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian shares out-perform in domestic market.
newsitem.headline: Australian shares out-perform in domestic market.

text.p: Shares continued to out-perform other asset classes in the Australian market in the year to March, producing a pre-tax rate of return of about 13.4 percent, ANZ Funds Management said in a quarterly report issued on Sunday.
Gold was the worst performing asset, tumbling 11.4 percent.
Fixed interest returned 12.4 percent, international shares 9.6 percent in Australian dollar terms, and cash 6.6 percent.
Australian residential property returned 17.1 percent over the period, with the Sydney and Melbourne markets returning 29.1 percent and 16 percent respectively.
Real rates of return - which take into account inflation - had been quite healthy for the past five years in each of the major asset classes, ANZ Funds Management said.

Shares continued to provide the best investment returns over five years, returning 13.3 percent compared with 12.9 percent for international shares. Fixed interest investments returned 9.6 percent, Australian property 9.9 percent and cash 6.4 percent.

On an after-tax basis, pooled superannuation funds, which invest in a mix of assets, achieved an 11 percent return over the year. For five and 10-year periods, superannuation funds returned 10.3 percent and eight percent respectively.
ANZ Funds Management's chief investment officer, Glenn Woolley, said gold continued to be plagued by low inflation.
"Over the past five years, investors have come to realise low inflation is here to stay in the long-term and, consequently, the gold price has recorded a zero return during this time," he said.
